Outcome: Efficacy of preventive therapy based on IGRA test results
Predictive value of IGRA for active TB
Correlation between IGRA positivity and occupational TB exposure
Principal Findings: 1) T-SPOT.TB: No studies evaluated T-SPOT.TB 2) QFT: All 5 comparisons gave positive estimates for the association between test positivity and occupational exposure (OR=1.28-4.15), 3/5 reached statistical significance. 3) TST: All 5 comparisons gave positive effect estimates (OR=1.33-5.09), 2/5 reached statistical significance.
What do these findings mean?: Data were limited on T-SPOT.TB and from low and middle income settings. Occupational exposure was associated with positivity for both tests, although this was not always significant. There is no strong evidence that IGRAs are more strongly correlated with occupational TB exposure than TST.

Outcome: Correlation between IGRA conversions and occupational TB exposure
Sensitivity for active TB (as a surrogate reference standard for LTBI)

Principal Findings: In low and middle income studies, agreement between IGRA and TST results ranged from 50.2%-81.4%. While IGRA consistently estimated a lower rate, this difference was significant in only 2/4 cases.
What do these findings mean?: Concordance was fair to poor in low and middle income settings. Both tests provide similar estimates of prevalence in low and middle income countries.

Outcome: Concordance between IGRA and TST conversions
Principal Findings: This study found 96% agreement between test conversions (QFT & TST).
What do these findings mean?: IGRA and TST conversions show moderate concordance. Data are limited in all settings.
